messages:
maria: Heads-up — I have a consistent repro for a pagewalk/pagetable misalignment on MI250x during long-context paged-attn runs. Fragmentation & KV reuse holes grow steadily and we hit OOM after ~1.2M tokens on batch=8.

kenji: Can you paste the minimal repro + any logs? is this tied to tiling kernel selection?

maria: Repro command: `python tools/repro_longctx.py --model redwood-1-3b --seq 32768 --gpu mi250x --batch 8 --iters 120000`
Logs (trimmed):
```
[2026-02-18 13:02:15] kvcache: alloc page idx=0x7f3a size=65536 owner=pid1234
[2026-02-18 13:02:17] pagetable: map slot=0x1a -> pte=0xABCDEF (tiling=Y)
[2026-02-18 13:02:18] evict: candidate range (slot 0x1a - 0x2f) overlap=TRUE
[2026-02-18 13:02:18] pagewalk: unexpected hole count +23
[2026-02-18 13:02:19] kvcache: reuse miss ++
```

maria: I attached a perf trace: https://perf.redwood/runs/1769823456 (flamegraph shows long tail in `paged_kernel_tile_dispatch` on MI250x). On H100 same workload the tiling kernel is never picked because of kernel selector heuristics and we don't hit the fragmentation/OOM.

dave: Interesting. sounds like the kernel selector prefers tiled kernels on MI250x for seq>16k which aligns different buffer/page offsets. Could be alignment mismatch where a tile spans multiple PT entries and our eviction granularity assumes per-entry atomicity.

olivia: FWIW I saw a similar pattern where NV vs AMD driver page alignments differ by 64B vs 256B for our tiled layout. ascii: `|PT-E|PT-E|PT-E|` vs tiled kernel window `|----tile----|` which can cross 2 PT-E boundaries. if eviction scans expect tile-contained-in-entry, they miss partial overlap -> ghost holes.

kenji: Can you try forcing the kernel selector to pick the untiled path? e.g. env `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=scalar_no_tile` or toggle `kernelselect.threshold.longseq=1e6` in canary config. If fragmentation disappears, that's a strong signal.

maria: I tried that. With `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=scalar_no_tile` OOM didn't happen for same token count. With tiled kernel we see steady growth rate ~+10MB/min.

perf-bot: CI reg: perf/regression: longctx-pagedattn MI250x +12% memory growth over baseline (see run 1769823456).

dave: Hypothesis: two issues combined — (1) kernel tiling fosters cross-PT entry writes that our page-table owner/refcounts don't account for; (2) eviction path assumes LRU/coalesce at PT-entry granularity, so partial writes create unreachable fragments. Could also be a mis-ordered prefetch that touches a page before owner is published (race).

kenji: Patch suggestion: add atomic update to PT owner publish and a conservative coalesce pass that merges adjacent partial slots before marking free. Small diff: `atomic_exchange(&pte->owner, new_owner)` before tiled-kernel dispatch, and barrier/flush on completion. Also add an assert in debug builds to detect partial-coverage writes.

olivia: Also try altering `kernelselect` to prefer non-tiling if `seq_len > 20k && gpu_vendor == amd` as a temporary mitigation. We'll need perf tradeoffs but better than OOM.

maria: I've uploaded a lightweight repro script + trace: `s3://redwood-debug/mi250x/pagedattn/1769823456/repro.tar.gz`. Repro notes: run on driver `rocm-5.6`, firmware `mi250x-v2`. Repro is deterministic across 3 runs on the same node.

dave: I'll put together a canary PR with the owner-publish change + kernel selector tweak. @kenji please review PT coalesce logic. If we get green on CI + no mem growth on MI250x longctx runs we can backport to the stable branch.

kenji: Ack. I'll also add a unit test that simulates partial-tile writes into adjacent PT entries and checks that the reclaimer doesn't drop coverage.

maria: Action items: dave -> PR owner-publish + selector canary; kenji -> coalesce unit test; olivia -> bench perf delta for scalar_no_tile fallback. I'll run a 24h longctx soak on mi250x once PR lands.

maria: tagging this as P0 for now until mitigation is in canary. :warning:
